Loki, the trickster god, a shape-shifter whose schemes both aid and threaten the Aesir. He was born a giant but accepted into the gods' company through oath-brotherhood with Odin, making him both insider and outsider within the divine realm.

Loki is a master of shape-shifting and illusion who can change his form and sex, allowing him to infiltrate and manipulate both gods and giants. This shape-shifting ability makes him a boundary-crosser who exists in multiple roles simultaneously. He represents the necessary chaos within order, the figure who reveals uncomfortable truths and tests the gods' limits.

He is directly responsible for the death of Balder by tricking the blind god Hod into throwing the mistletoe dart that kills the beloved. This act breaks the peace of the gods and sets the chain of events toward Ragnarok in motion. Yet despite his destructive schemes, Loki's trickery often results in the gods acquiring their greatest treasures. He was involved in the creation of Gungnir, the spear that never misses. He helped bring about the forging of Mjolnir, Thor's mighty hammer. He orchestrated the making of Draupnir, the golden ring that drips riches. All of these priceless artifacts exist because of his scheming.

Loki is father to three monstrous children destined to fight against the gods at Ragnarok: Fenrir the wolf, Jormungandr the World Serpent, and Hel the death goddess. As punishment for his betrayals, Loki was bound under the earth with a serpent dripping venom on his face. But he will break free at the end of all things to lead the forces of chaos against the gods. He is Heimdall's final opponent, the watchman's eternal antagonist, and his ultimate confrontation with Heimdall will seal the fate of worlds.
